response.explanation: The old code called self.process.kill() unconditionally. The new code only calls kill() when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. That class derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.context.Process` (what `multiprocessing.Process` refers to). The isinstance check is therefore False for every real production process. When a process is detected as "hang" (alive but not updating healthy_since), kill() is skipped, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second process for the same shards while the hung one stays alive. The same check is used in join() before process.terminate() (line 346), so real processes are not terminated there either.
response.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process fails for SpawnProcess
